newsitem.title: UK: CBI wants advisers for UK utilities regulators.
newsitem.headline: CBI wants advisers for UK utilities regulators.

text.p: Britain's Confederation of British Industry (CBI) on Friday proposed the setting-up of advisory boards to regulate the activities of utilities regulators.
CBI deputy director-general Peter Agar said he had become concerned that regulaton had become "rather too individualised or personalised".
In a discussion paper, the CBI said it had concluded that it would be positive to remove the concentration of discretionary power from the hands of a single individual.
It proposed that standing panels of advisers could debate intricate issues, giving consumers an assurance that decisions had been made after taking into account a range of views.
"The panel might be required to to publish its advice and the regulator required to publish reasons where that advice is not taken up," the paper says.
But Agar expressed himself against a "super regulator" which he said would introduce an intolerable extra layer of bureaucracy.

The CBI is also against a Labour Party plan for a windfall tax. "It's not good business to impose retrospective taxation," Agar told a press briefing. "It makes planning difficult and would undermine incentives to produce efficiencies." -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
